<!-- ============ INTERACTIVE MYSTERY ============ -->
<h2 class="cba-h">Try your first mystery</h2>
<p class="cba-sub">No sign-up, no setup. Make one decision and see how a computational biologist actually thinks.</p>

<div class="cba-mystery" id="cba-mystery">
  <div class="head">
    <span class="title">Your first mystery</span>
    <span class="pill">30-SECOND CHALLENGE</span>
  </div>
  <div class="body">
    <p class="prompt">Prof. Zola has just dropped a sequencing file on your desk:</p>
    <p><span class="file">tumor_sample_R1.fastq.gz</span></p>
    <p class="quote">"Find out which genes are differentially expressed. I need results by Friday." <span class="who">— Prof. Zola</span></p>
    <p class="ask">What should you do first?</p>

    <button class="cba-opt" data-correct="false"
      data-why="Tempting, but you have no idea yet whether the reads are any good, or even what you are comparing against. Garbage in, garbage out.">
      Run differential expression analysis immediately
    </button>
    <button class="cba-opt" data-correct="true"
      data-why="Exactly. Before any analysis, you inspect read quality and understand the study design: what are the groups, the replicates, the comparison? This one habit separates results you can defend from results you cannot.">
      Check the sequencing data quality and the study design
    </button>
    <button class="cba-opt" data-correct="false"
      data-why="Volcano plots are lovely, but a plot built on unchecked data and an unknown comparison answers no biological question.">
      Make a volcano plot. Scientists love volcano plots.
    </button>

    <div class="outcome" id="cba-outcome">
      <p><strong>That is the Academy way.</strong> Every module starts with a question, not a command. You will learn to earn each result before you trust it.</p>
      <p><a class="btn btn-primary" href="modules/05-reads-and-quality-control/" role="button">See how we check data quality →</a></p>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>

<section class="cba-band cba-philosophy">
The best way to learn computational biology is not by memorizing commands. It is by asking biological questions. Everything here follows from that one idea.
</section>

<!-- ============ THREE LEARNING MODES ============ -->
<h2 class="cba-h" id="modes">Three ways to learn</h2>
<p class="cba-sub">These are learning modes, not levels you graduate from. Beginners can start asking real questions on day one, and experienced researchers can drop back to shore up a foundation.</p>
<div class="cba-modes">
  <div class="cba-mode">
    <div class="step">Explore</div>
    <div class="name">Explore</div>
    <p class="desc">Understand biology, data, and the essential tools: the terminal, R, Conda, and the file formats everything else is built on.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="cba-mode">
    <div class="step">Investigate</div>
    <div class="name">Investigate</div>
    <p class="desc">Analyze real data and interpret the evidence: quality control, alignment, variants, quantification, and automation.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="cba-mode">
    <div class="step">Discover</div>
    <div class="name">Discover</div>
    <p class="desc">Design studies and generate new insight: differential expression, single-cell, and spatial biology.</p>
  </div>
</div>

<!-- ============ RESEARCH JOURNEY ============ -->
<section class="cba-band">
<h3>The lab's first research project</h3>
<p>You join a lab, the data arrives, and you take it all the way. Follow one experiment from raw data to a defensible scientific conclusion.</p>
<ol class="cba-journey">
  <li><span class="q">The samples arrive.</span> <span class="a">Understand the study design and metadata.</span></li>
  <li><span class="q">Can we trust the data?</span> <span class="a">Inspect quality and identify problems before analysis.</span></li>
  <li><span class="q">What changed?</span> <span class="a">Quantify and compare gene expression between groups.</span></li>
  <li><span class="q">Does it make biological sense?</span> <span class="a">Interpret pathways and validate the conclusion.</span></li>
  <li><span class="q">Can someone reproduce it?</span> <span class="a">Package the workflow, figures, and methods.</span></li>
</ol>
<p class="cba-sub" style="margin-top:0.9rem"><strong>A note on honesty:</strong> the single-cell and spatial modules use their own datasets suited to those methods. They are not treated as automatic downstream products of one bulk RNA-seq run, because in real science they would not be.</p>
</section>

<!-- ============ EVERY MODULE IS A STORY ============ -->
<h2 class="cba-h">Every module is a story</h2>
<p class="cba-sub">The same shape every time, so it never feels random: a complete, self-contained journey from a question to an answer you can defend.</p>
<div class="cba-steps">
  <span class="chip">🧩 Start with a mystery</span>
  <span class="chip">🤔 Think first</span>
  <span class="chip">💬 Story</span>

  <span class="chip">🎉 What just happened</span>
  <span class="chip">⚠️ Common mistakes</span>
  <span class="chip">🧩 Mini challenge</span>
  <span class="chip">🎯 Key takeaway</span>
</div>

<section class="cba-band" style="text-align:center">
<h3>Teach why before how. Always.</h3>
<p style="opacity:0.85;max-width:60ch;margin:0.4rem auto 0">Anyone can copy a command. We want you to know what question it answers, and why the answer matters. That is the whole difference between running software and doing science.</p>
</section>

<script>
(function () {
  // --- Interactive mystery ---
  var mystery = document.getElementById('cba-mystery');
  if (mystery) {
    var opts = mystery.querySelectorAll('.cba-opt');
    var outcome = document.getElementById('cba-outcome');
    opts.forEach(function (btn) {
      btn.addEventListener('click', function () {
        if (btn.querySelector('.verdict')) return; // already answered
        var correct = btn.getAttribute('data-correct') === 'true';
        btn.classList.add(correct ? 'correct' : 'wrong');
        var v = document.createElement('span');
        v.className = 'verdict';
        v.textContent = (correct ? '✓ ' : '✗ ') + btn.getAttribute('data-why');
        btn.appendChild(v);
        if (correct && outcome) outcome.classList.add('show');
      });
    });
  }
  // --- Module filter ---
  var filter = document.getElementById('cba-filter');
  var grid = document.getElementById('cba-grid');
  if (filter && grid) {
    var cards = grid.querySelectorAll('.cba-modcard');
    filter.querySelectorAll('button').forEach(function (b) {
      b.addEventListener('click', function () {
        filter.querySelectorAll('button').forEach(function (x) { x.classList.remove('active'); });
        b.classList.add('active');
        var f = b.getAttribute('data-filter');
        cards.forEach(function (c) {
          c.hidden = !(f === 'all' || c.getAttribute('data-mode') === f);
        });
      });
    });
  }
})();
</script>
